title.narrative: El Salvador Transport and Resilient Infrastructure Project

description.narrative: The US$150 million El Salvador Transport and Resilient Infrastructure Project was approved by the Board on October 30, 2023, and became effective on May 16, 2024. The current closing date is December 28, 2029. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is: “to (i) improve resilient connectivity in targeted areas of the Northern Metropolitan Area of San Salvador, (ii) enhance sustainable national road sector management and (iii) in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it”. The Project includes the following four components: (i) Connectivity Improvement for the Northern Metropolitan Area of San Salvador; (ii) Institutional Capacity Building for Climate-Resilient, Safe and Inclusive Road Infrastructure; (iii) Project Management; and (iv) Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC).Component 1: Connectivity Improvement for the Northern Metropolitan Area of San Salvador (Original: US134.05million; Revised: US251.5million). This component seeks to strengthen road infrastructure in the Northern Metropolitan Area of San Salvador by building a road bypass and implementing complementary road safety and resilient connectivity interventions in the area. The road bypass infrastructure consists of a 13.05 km greenfield road that includes 13 bridges. It will connect the SAL38 highway (Carretera de Oro) and CA-4 (Carretera Troncal de Norte) (See map below). The largest structure to be built is a 400 m bridge with a 320 m span cable-stayed structure to connect the bypass infrastructure to the bypass accesses over the existing SAL38 highway.Component 2: Institutional Capacity Building for Climate-Resilient, Safe and Inclusive Road Infrastructure Original: US$3.45 million; Revised: US$6.00 million). This component will implement capacity-building activities to strengthen GoES institutional capacity in managing the national road network, including: (a) Design studies for sustainable and resilient road projects; (b) Support for the planning of resilient of road infrastructure; (c) Institutional and capacity building in road safety; (e) Development of an Integrated Manual on climate-resilience, road safety and inclusiveness standards; (f) Support to mobilize private capital for road development; (g) Promotion of gender equality in the road sector; (h) Support for the use of unmanned aircraft systems, or drones, for monitoring road networks and preventing natural hazard risks. Component 3: Project Management (US$3.8 million). This subcomponent provides support for project management and coordination, fiduciary administration, E&S, Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) and training.Component 4: Contingency Emergency Response (Original: US$0 million; Revised: US$8.7 million). This component enables the GoES to respond swiftly and effectively to eligible crisis or emergencies. On June 16, 2024, following heavy rains and storms hit the country due to the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), the GoES declared the state of emergency (Legislative Decree N°28). The Bank received two letters from the Borrower's Ministry of Finance on June 19, 2024, and on October 31, 2024, respectively, requesting the activation of the CERC to finance infrastructure rehabilitation activities to address the impacts of the ITCZ for US$8.7 million. The activity to be financed by the CERC is the rehabilitation of the riverbank and edges of the Rio Grande de San Miguel for the recovery of livelihoods in the Canton La Canoa, District of San Miguel, Municipality of San Miguel Centro, Department of San Miguel — one of the areas more severely impacted by the intense rainfall in the Borrower's territory in June 2024 —. The infrastructure works will include: (i) rehabilitation of the riverbank and edges, using select material mechanically compacted to protect the road, homes and crop areas; and (ii) erosion control works along the riverbank. Following the request, the CERC was activated by the Bank on December 13, 2024. The MOPT is carrying out the internal processes for: (i) prepare the bidding documents to initiate the works, and (ii) authorize the disbursement request.An Additional Financing (AF) is being processed to support activities already included in the parent Projects design and consistent with the PDO. The proposed Additional Finance (AF) of US$120 million aims to: (a) address the financing gap due to the shortfall in counterpart funding for the SAL38 bridge; (b) increase the budget allocated to complementary works on the access roads to the bypass and its surroundings; (c) increase the budget allocated for institutional capacity building activities; and (d) replenish the allocation to the CERC component.

To (i) improve resilient and safe connectivity around Apopa in northern Metropolitan Area of San Salvador, (ii) enhance sustainable national road sector management and (iii) in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.
